title: Kanva Dynasty
capsule: The Kanva dynasty was a Brahmin ruling house of Magadha founded c. 73 BCE when the minister Vasudeva Kanva assassinated the last Shunga emperor Devabhuti and assumed the throne at Pataliputra. The dynasty comprised only four rulers — Vasudeva, Bhumimitra, Narayana, and Susarman — and lasted until approximately 28 BCE, when the Satavahana ruler Simuka overthrew Susarman and ended Kanva power. The Kanvas controlled Magadha proper but appear to have exercised little authority over the peripheral territories the Shungas had nominally held, representing a period of political contraction in northern India.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The dynasty is known almost entirely from Puranic king-lists and a handful of copper-plate inscriptions; the territorial extent of Kanva authority is conjectural and likely limited to the Gangetic heartland.
